text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to $150.80, extending a two-week rally of over 12%, as oil prices surged on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude hit $116 a barrel—a six-month high—following Saudi Arabia's interception of Houthi missiles and drones, combined with Trump administration rhetoric about potential military action against Iran. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to higher profits from both upstream production and refining operations.

The move fits into a broader rally in energy stocks as geopolitical risk in the Middle East tightens global oil supply. When regional tensions spike and traders worry about disruptions to a major oil-producing region, crude prices climb, and integrated energy companies benefit from the margin expansion—they produce and sell at elevated prices while their costs don't move dollar-for-dollar upward.
